structured_output.what_is_happening: T/ACC ("Technology Accelerationist") is a pump.fun coin about 2.7 hours old and still on its bonding curve (86.5 of about 115 virtual SOL). Market cap is about $28k. It is up about 7x over 6h and about 135% over 1h, and it sits about 11% below its all-time high. The coin is labeled a community takeover. Its X link is an old Elon Musk status, its website is an X community, and its description is "Fees to @elonmusk via UsePaid", a celebrity fee-routing gimmick. The original creator has left (creator_close, 0 balance). There were 182 unique buyers in the last hour against 101 sellers, and hourly volume is about 1x market cap. The last 5 minutes show slight cooling (-3 to -6%, buys and sells about even). GMGN tags 97 of 200 traders as bundlers (top bundler trader share 27.8%) and 73 as fresh wallets.

narrative.description: t/acc (technology accelerationism) is a recognizable tech-right meme term that Elon Musk has echoed. The token pairs it with an old Musk post and a 'fees to Elon' mechanic, a recurring pump.fun template. There is no fresh catalyst in the packet. The link points to a tweet from 2024, not a new post.
narrative.why_spreading: It rides a known Musk-adjacent term plus the fee-to-celebrity trend. The community takeover after the dev left drew a wave of buyers. With no new Musk post, it is mostly momentum on the curve.

token_connection.why_this_token: It is the only live t/acc token. The packet's one other same-name token has 0 liquidity and was created months earlier.

authenticity.evidence: Unique-buyer breadth is decent: 182 buyers per hour, 431 over 6h, and 359 holders, with top-10 at about 27% excluding the curve. There is no paid DexScreener ad or boost. Against that, 97 of 200 traders are tagged bundlers with a top bundler trader share of 27.8%, the bot/degen rate is 35%, and fresh wallets number 73. The DexScreener profile was updated under a community takeover, which is organized promotion.
authenticity.uncertainty: The bundler tag may cover the CTO group's coordinated buys rather than dev insiders. It is unclear whether bundlers are still holding or already distributing.
